title: Linguocognitive specifics of visual communication (based on material from German-language public social networks)
text_snippet: Linguocognitive specifics of visual communication (based on material from German-language public social networks) The article examines the linguocognitive specifics of German-language visual communication within institutional and everyday contexts. The research material consists of fragments of authentic correspondence in German presented on public German-language social networks. The study employs elements of discourse and content analysis, as well as contextual and linguosemiotic analysis methods. The relevance of the research is determined by the objective need to study trends in the development of the German language amidst digital transformations and the integration of artificial intelligence; to establish the specifics of sociocultural interaction in professional spheres and everyday situations; and to identify the features of linguistic-creative activity among participants in visual communication. As a result of analyzing the empirical material in German, it was established that the virtual environment stimulates the development of inclusive communication, promotes an “iconic” shift in public social networks, facilitates the simplification of norms and rules in modern German, and supports network forms of communication in both everyday and institutional settings. title: Cognitive and communicative strategies for construction an intra-event perspective: gerundial constructions in English discourse
text_snippet: Cognitive and communicative strategies for construction an intra-event perspective: gerundial constructions in English discourse Within the framework of the modern cognitive and discursive paradigm of linguistic knowledge, this article investigates the mental and pragmatic mechanisms underlying the functioning of gerundial constructions in the position of verbal complementation. Drawing on data from representative synchronous English corpora (Brown University Corpus and Lancaster-Oslo/Bergen Corpus), the authors deconstruct the classical structuralist, rigid temporal, and narrow referential explanatory models of verbal variation, demonstrating their internal theoretical inconsistency in natural language usage. As a novel research perspective, a holistic model is proposed that conceptualizes the syntactic pattern [Subject + LIKE + V-ing] as an independent symbolic unit – a construction whose invariant semantic value is deeply embedded within the syntactic matrix. For the first time, the gerundial complement is conceptualized as an instrument of conceptual reification of the Experiencer’s processual experience, shifting the human cognitive system from sequential scanning to summary scanning. title: Comparative analysis of stand-up comedy means (based on Russian and Indonesian linguistic cultures)
text_snippet: Comparative analysis of stand-up comedy means (based on Russian and Indonesian linguistic cultures) This article presents a comparative study of comic means employed in Russian and Indonesian stand-up comedy. Performances by Russian and Indonesian stand-up comedians representing different ethnic groups in the framework of the above-mentioned cultures, as reflected in their work, were used as a source material to identify comic means. Another factor influencing the choice of artists was the discussion of pressing social issues in their comedy routines, using a wide range of linguistic devices. The linguistic and axiological method is employed since it provides the opportunity to describe the value and anti-value components of the standup-comedy genre and those socio-political matters that become the topic for humorous discussion. The comedic means used in both cultures can be divided into two groups. The first group includes means based on the absurdity of the situation, as well as the ontological juxtaposition of a real-life situation and its humorous interpretation. The second group includes comedy means based on language game. title: Interpretive structure transformation of the stative concept MUST in the community collective consciousness
text_snippet: Interpretive structure transformation of the stative concept MUST in the community collective consciousness The paper explores the cognitive and semantic transformation mechanisms of the interpretation nuclear field of the stative concept MUST, which demonstrates its universal character in various linguistic cultures. In the framework of this study, microcontexts are analyzed that illustrate the semantic dynamics of the transformation of the lexemes must, duty, and obligation as basic verbalizers of the concept under consideration, demonstrating the development trajectory of the derogative component of interpretation in the process of macrodiachronic sacred, philosophical, moral, ethical, and individualistic narrativization. Methodologically, the research is based on a combination of linguistic and axiological, diachronic and conceptual, as well as dialectical and relational analysis, which allows us to show how the axiological significance of the elements of a concept varies depending on the dominant epistemological paradigm and consituative determinants. title: Gender specificity of the associative field of the concept CULTURE in Russian linguistic consciousness
text_snippet: Gender specificity of the associative field of the concept CULTURE in Russian linguistic consciousness The paper explores the cognitive modeling of the concept CULTURE in the linguistic consciousness of Russian youth. The aim of the study is to empirically examine the current structure of the associative field of the concept CULTURE and identify the gender specifics of its perception. The research methods include a free association experiment, content analysis for the semantic categorization of responses, a method of layered division of the associative field with the identification of core, basic, and peripheral layers, as well as quantitative and qualitative analysis of the obtained data, taking into account the gender factor. The empirical part was based on 606 respondents (390 men and 216 women). Through content analysis and layered division of the associative field, 13 thematic groups (clusters) were identified and classified, and their frequency hierarchy was determined. A quantitative and qualitative analysis of the data revealed that the core of the general associative field is formed by the thematic groups “Creative Arts”, “Axiological and Subjective-Evaluative Component”, and “National and Geocultural Specifics”. title: The role of conceptual metaphor in the discursive interpretation of English-language psychology blogs
text_snippet: The role of conceptual metaphor in the discursive interpretation of English-language psychology blogs This paper examines the specific features of discursive interpretation using English-language psychology blogs as a case study. The relevance of the study stems from the insufficient scholarly attention paid to psychology blogs from a cognitive-discursive perspective, which is essential for understanding how information embedded in such texts is encoded and decoded. The aim of this work is to demonstrate that discursive interpretation facilitates the comprehension and reconstruction of the blogger’s intent — specifically, the structuring of their own thoughts and the provision of self-help tools for readers. The research employs a set of general scientific methods (analysis, synthesis, generalization) alongside techniques from cognitive linguistics, including conceptual and definitional analysis, contextual analysis, and elements of cognitive modelling. The study reveals the role of the cognitive mechanism “conceptual metaphor” in facilitating discursive interpretation. By translating abstract concepts into concrete-sensory ones, this mechanism allows the author to exert covert influence on the reader and model their behavior. title: Equivalent text cognitive dominant WAR-KRIEG in the mnemic narratives of M. A. Sholokhov and E. M. Remarque
text_snippet: Equivalent text cognitive dominant WAR-KRIEG in the mnemic narratives of M. A. Sholokhov and E. M. Remarque The paper examines the architectonics of the equivalent text cognitive dominant WAR-KRIEG created in the works of M. A. Sholokhov and E. M. Remarque dedicated to World War II. The aim of the study is to identify the literary concepts characteristic for this cognitive dominant. Using the method of cognitive and hermeneutic modeling the following equivalent literary concepts were identified: PRIRODA-NATURE, VOINA-KRIEG, and SMERT-TOD. A comparative and contrastive method made it possible to identify the relationship between equivalent concepts in the two works: in the story “The Science of Hatred,” the most frequent literary concept is PRIRODA (NATURE), the least frequent is SMERT (DEATH). In the novel “Zeit zu lieben und Zeit zu sterben,” the most frequent literary concept is TOD, the least frequent is KRIEG. The choice of texts for analysis was determined by the following factors: both works are about the Great Patriotic War and represent the views of German and Russian soldiers on the same events. title: Knowledge representation in educational texts (based on English language material)
text_snippet: Knowledge representation in educational texts (based on English language material) The paper aims to analyze the linguistic means of knowledge representation in educational texts for different education levels. These means demonstrate how educational text interprets knowledge about the world in a specific subject area. The study employs methods of conceptual and interpretative analysis, semantic, contextual, and structural text analysis. The material used is English Math texts for primary, secondary, and high education levels. The study identifies lexical, grammatical, and structural and semantic differences in knowledge representation in these educational texts. Texts for the primary level represent the basics of mathematical knowledge, which is based on general knowledge. The vocabulary used is simple in structure and semantics. The use of terms is limited, and their meaning is explained by the words of general semantics. The texts use simple morphological forms and simple, short sentences. Texts for the secondary school level contain a greater number of mathematical terms explained by special vocabulary, complex morphological forms, and complex sentences. title: The cognitive and discursive potential of generational neologisms: selection criteria for reconstructing cohort code and discursive age
text_snippet: The cognitive and discursive potential of generational neologisms: selection criteria for reconstructing cohort code and discursive age The article addresses the problem of distinguishing generational neologisms from general-language innovations, since neither the novelty of a lexical unit nor its association with a particular age group is in itself sufficient to establish its generational significance. The aim of the study is to develop a system of criteria for selecting generational neologisms that have the potential to reconstruct cohort code and discursive age. The theoretical framework is based on the model of the linguistic genetics of generations, which integrates the cognitive and axiological, communicative, and lexical levels of the representation of generational experience. The material comprises 30 contexts in which the neologism tradwife is used, drawn from Urban Dictionary, The Guardian, Time, Vogue, The Washington Post, AP News (Cambridge Dictionary), and Reddit. The methodology combines contextual-interpretative, cognitive, axiological, pragmatic, and discourse analysis. title: Cognitive and discursive perspectives of grammatical neologization
text_snippet: Cognitive and discursive perspectives of grammatical neologization The article examines the vectors of grammatical neologization of the modern Russian literary language within the framework of the communicative-cognitive approach, based on the material of journalistic texts of the mass media and data from the Russian National Corpus. The mechanisms of neosememe generation and their structural and grammatical consequences at the intersection of lexical and grammatical subsystems are considered. Based on the analysis of the processes of repeated substantivation, gradual transition of relative adjectives into qualitative ones, transitivization/intransitivization of verb vocabulary, as well as transformations of abstract, concrete and collective nouns, a large-scale zone of lexico-grammatical syncretism is explicated. It is proved that the discursive conditions of modern media systems and pragmatic factors (including the law of speech economy) act as a key driver of the restructuring of morphological categories and syntactic valencies of words.

title: Systematization principles of motivational discourse genres
text_snippet: Systematization principles of motivational discourse genres Modern communication between people who are focused on making only informed decisions requires defining the principles of forming strategies that can change the views of the audience. In this regard, the description of the motivational discourse features, specifically designed for emotional impact on the addressee, and the development of a concept for constructing its genres for subsequent implementation in the education of students of relevant specialties seems to be very relevant. The purpose of the study is to systematize the genres of motivational discourse so that in the future it would be possible to determine the place in the general system of each new phenomenon that falls within the circle of interests of scientists. The material for the study was 64 motivational speeches related to different types of discourse, which were studied using rhetorical, contextual and discourse analysis. The systematization was carried out according to two parameters. The first is the criterion of “type of speech by purpose”. title: Linguacognitive markers of hedging epistemic responsibility in fake discourse
text_snippet: Linguacognitive markers of hedging epistemic responsibility in fake discourse This study identifies and analyzes the functional and pragmatic potential of linguacognitive markers of hedging epistemic responsibility in quasi‑factual informational media discourse. The dominant principle underlying the transition from obligatory aletics to facultative aletics – which creates the domain of factoid representation of falsehood and the transition of attractive hedonicity into informational and operational manipulation – is the convergence of inferential evidentiality and epistemic necessity based on the translation and mimetization of the frame of certainty. A comprehensive analysis methodology based on inferential selection and lemmatization of tokens, followed by the formation of a representative corpus of fake micro‑contexts, dialectical and relational analysis of the illocutionary intention of factualizing false information, and functional and pragmatic analysis of hedging constructions, ensures the reliability of the research results. title: Institutional conditionality of tonality in regional media (communicative and pragmatic aspect)
text_snippet: Institutional conditionality of tonality in regional media (communicative and pragmatic aspect) The paper examines the influence of the institutional affiliation of regional media outlets on their tone and, consequently, their influence on readers. This study employs a communicative and pragmatic approach, which considers the tone of media texts not simply as an element of style, but as a key mechanism conveying editorial position and aimed at achieving a specific verbal and conceptual outcome. The relevance of this study is due to its attempt to establish a connection between the type of media organization (state, private news, or expert-analytical) and the use of linguistic, syntactic, and structural techniques that determine a specific form of interaction with readers. The analysis was conducted on materials published by three key publications in the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia): the state information agency “YSIA”, the private news portal “SakhaDay” and the expert-analytical portal “Regional Comments.” The study period covers 2024 to 2026. The study utilized methods of discourse analysis, contextual and stylistic analysis, and elements of component analysis when working with emotive vocabulary. title: Professional and combat experience in conceptualizing the military domain: a psycholinguistic study
text_snippet: Professional and combat experience in conceptualizing the military domain: a psycholinguistic study The article explores intracultural variations in the military domain conceptualization depending on respondents’ professional and combat involvement degree. The relevance lies in the fact that professional socialization and direct combat experience may be associated with differences in the organization of conceptual content among speakers of one linguaculture; however, the nature of differences in the military domain remains insufficiently explored. The study involved 300 Russian speakers divided into three equal groups: civilians, military personnel without combat experience and participants in the Special Military Operation. A directed associative experiment and a semantic differential were used. The analysis focused on four concepts – ARMY, WEAPON, SECURITY and FEAR – representing institutional, operational, value-related and emotional components of the military conceptual sphere. It was determined that shared semantic components were preserved across all groups, while their relative salience and organization differed. title: Discursive functions of 18th-century intertextual inclusions in the song “Rime of the Ancient Mariner” by Iron Maiden
text_snippet: Discursive functions of 18th-century intertextual inclusions in the song “Rime of the Ancient Mariner” by Iron Maiden Song discourse exerts a significant emotional impact on the recipient, serving as an important channel for transmitting cultural meanings. The relevance of the study is due to the necessity to examine intertextual inclusions as means of foregrounding semantic and cognitive dominants in song lyrics. The aim of the research is to identify the discursive functions of intertextual inclusions from S.T. Coleridge’s poem “The Rime of the Ancient Mariner” (18th century) in the eponymous song by Iron Maiden. The material for the study is the lyrics of the composition, which contain quotations from the poem. During the research the methods of discourse analysis, linguacognitive analysis were employed. Observation and description techniques were also used. Consequently, two main discursive functions performed by intertextual inclusions in the song text were identified: expressive and detailing, which are subtypes of the axiological and cognitive discursive functions proposed by I. Kasavin. title: Beyond corpus linguistics: integrating methods in cognitive research
text_snippet: Beyond corpus linguistics: integrating methods in cognitive research Overall, the article addresses the limitations of corpus analysis, which despite its representativeness and objectivity captures only the manifestations of speech without providing access to the mental processes behind language. The aim is to systematize and typologize approaches to overcome these limitations and to substantiate converging evidence as a tool for enhancing reliability. The paper proposes a typology of six main approaches grouped by their relation to corpus analysis: semantic-cognitive and experimental methods expand the empirical basis; usage‑based and parametric approaches shift the theoretical perspective; conceptual‑inferential and ecological cognitive linguistics broaden the research perspective. The typology is tested on the concept SUCCESS in Russian consciousness using data from the Russian Associative Dictionary, the National Corpus, and psychosemantic and associative experiments. Comparison of corpus and experimental data revealed a core and peripheral shifts. Corpus analysis showed an increase in collocations for active achievement, while associative experiments also revealed a shift from luck as a gift to success as a result of overcoming obstacles. title: Sociocultural code models of modularly integrated cognitive information constructs in R. Stevenson’s and T. Fontane’s novels
text_snippet: Sociocultural code models of modularly integrated cognitive information constructs in R. Stevenson’s and T. Fontane’s novels The article studies dynamic cognitive constructs in multilingual works. Modularly integrated cognitive information constructs are considered as units in which text cognitive scenes and text cognitive scripts are interfaced. The author’s interpretative algorithm for constructing comparative proxemic code models of the background terminal of textual cognitive scenes, as well as linguistic analysis, comparative method, cognitive and hermeneutical analysis and quantitative analysis, is used as a research method. The features of the nonverbal communication markers included in the studied constructs are determined. It is noted that in the structure of the modularly integrated cognitive information construct, the text cognitive script is the background terminal of the text cognitive scene. In the course of the study, two multilingual temporally non-distant novels were considered, in which a high frequency of modularly integrated cognitive information constructs was revealed. Examination of the background terminal of the studied cognitive units revealed a large number of markers of the nonverbal communication code, which include proxemes, kinemes, chronemes, takemes, sensemes. title: Expressing the intensity of a characteristic through a comparative model: expressive aspect (based on the assessment of intellectual abilities)
text_snippet: Expressing the intensity of a characteristic through a comparative model: expressive aspect (based on the assessment of intellectual abilities) The article analyzes the functioning of the comparative model as a way to characterize the degree of human mental abilities manifestation. The relevance and novelty of the study lie in the need to identify systemic patterns in the creation of expressiveness that accompanies the expression of power meaning in speech. The aim of the paper is to analyze the possibilities and mechanism of creating expressiveness when expressing the intensity of a feature using the comparative model, which is embodied in the construction of the comparative turnover. The study is conducted using the example of characterizing the degree of manifestation of mental abilities called the adjectives “smart” and “stupid”, in combination with the construction of the comparative turnover. The material for the analysis is fragments of texts containing a power assessment of a person’s intellectual qualities, extracted from the resources of the National Corpus of the Russian Language. The study was conducted using the methods of component, contextual and stylistic analysis. title: Mechanisms of cognitive dissonance realization in English-language aphorisms
text_snippet: Mechanisms of cognitive dissonance realization in English-language aphorisms The English-language aphorism serves as an amphibolous tool for both establishing and reinforcing cognitive stereotypes within the collective consciousness and for deconstructing them. Authors of aphorisms combine disparate cognitive domains, link peripheral areas of the deep semantics associated with distinct concepts, and employ unconventional interpretations of both fundamental cultural and linguacultural concepts; this process can trigger cognitive dissonance during the initial stage of reception, prior to the full unpacking of meaning. This study analyzes the specific linguistic mechanisms underlying the cognitive dissonance that arises from aphoristic apothegms formation. The study focuses on the linguistic, discursive, and linguacognitive tools used to realize the pragmatic potential of dissonant constructions. The research material consists of aphorisms by English-language authors from the 19th and 20th centuries. The aim of the work is to identify the key mechanisms underlying the realization of cognitive dissonance at various linguistic levels. title: Discourse event in a 17th-century medical document (cognitive and communicative aspect)
text_snippet: Discourse event in a 17th-century medical document (cognitive and communicative aspect) This study is devoted to the diachronic analysis of medical document genres. The aim of the research is to examine the specific features of the formation of institutional medical discourse, to identify and describe discourse events in 17th‑century medical documents, and to determine their role in the development of professional communication. The research material comprises 847 documents extracted from the Apothecary Prikaz, housed in the Russian State Archive of Ancient Acts. The study employs methods of discourse analysis, historical‑linguistic description, genre analysis, and content analysis. It has been established that the documents of the Apothecary Prikaz constitute a developed genre system, comprising administrative (gramota, pamyat), reporting (otpiska, doklad), registration and accounting (rospis, spisok), petitionary (chelobitnaya) documents, and special medical documents (skazka, prescription). title: Russian colloquial particles in phatic communication models: an experience of corpus-assisted discourse studies
text_snippet: Russian colloquial particles in phatic communication models: an experience of corpus-assisted discourse studies The work presents the experience of corpus-assisted discourse studies of communicative strategies in various discursive practices of modern Russian native speakers. The aim of the study is to analyze the semantics and functions of Russian colloquial derivative particles based on interrogative-relative pronouns in phatic question-and-answer adjacency pairs based on corpus data. The methodology of cognitive-discursive analysis of corpus data was used. The material for the study is the author’s subcorpus of question-and-answer adjacency pairs extracted from the main corpus of the Russian National Corpus. The volume of the material is about 200 dialogic units of the question-answer type. Colloquial derivative particles based on interrogative-relative pronouns are considered (taking into account their structural variants): (da) chego (uzh) tam / tut; (da) kakoe (uzh) tam / tut; (da) gde (uzh) tam / tut and (da) kuda (uzh) tam / tut. A contensive interpretation of the semantic and pragmatic features of their verbal implementation, as well as their communicative functions in the organization of phatic speech interaction, is provided. title: Architectonics of the “patriot – traitor” opposition in the linguistic consciousness of the north Caucasus youth: markers of Russian identity
text_snippet: Architectonics of the “patriot – traitor” opposition in the linguistic consciousness of the north Caucasus youth: markers of Russian identity The study aims to explicate the linguacognitive structure and perform a semantic clustering of patriotic markers of Russian identity through the analysis of verbal associative reactions to the “patriot – traitor” binary opposition in the linguistic consciousness of the North Caucasus youth. Based on the analysis and semantic clustering of the associative field of the PATRIOT concept, a basic schema of its interiorization has been identified, revealing the following cognitive mechanism of forming the civic-patriotic vector of Russian identity in the youth’s linguistic consciousness: from a strong emotional and axiological objectification of the image of the Motherland, through the actualization of the archetypal characteristics of a warrior-defender, to the subsequent expansion of the conceptual space of patriotism by incorporating traditional spiritual values, and finally, reaching the level of a rational understanding of its civic-political projection. title: Conceptual and integrative model of the Ossetian phraseosystem as a hierarchy of cognitive strategies for encoding experience
text_snippet: Conceptual and integrative model of the Ossetian phraseosystem as a hierarchy of cognitive strategies for encoding experience The article is devoted to the development and verification of a conceptual and integrative model of the Ossetian phraseosystem representing the fundamental binary opposition “friend – foe”. The aim of the study is to describe the architectonics of the phraseological system of the Ossetian language as a hierarchy of four interrelated cognitive strategies for encoding ethnocultural experience: epistemological signification, axiological scaling, cross-domain mapping, and interdiscursive transfer. The relevance of the work is due to the need to overcome the limitations of descriptive, lexicographic and comparative approaches to Ossetian phraseology and to move towards cognitive and discursive modeling. The empirical basis consists of 182 phraseological units of the Ossetian language selected from lexicographic sources according to the semantic criterion of the presence of the “friend – foe” opposition (khion vs. ætsægælon), followed by corpus verification on texts with a total length of 8,028,980 word usages. title: Corpus analysis of discursive markers in consumer product advertising (In Eng.)
text_snippet: Corpus analysis of discursive markers in consumer product advertising (In Eng.) The study examines the problem of the functioning of discursive markers in advertising texts of consumer products on the Chinese Internet platform Pinduoduo. The relevance of the study is due to the insufficient knowledge of advertising texts in Chinese from the point of view of using language markers as a means of speech influence on recipients. Therefore, the main purpose of the work is to identify the functional and pragmatic features of discursive markers through corpus analysis. The authors have created a specialized corpus with a volume of 16,796 tokens based on text transcripts of 120 short videos advertising consumer goods selected from the platform. Video transcripts were generated via the Notta platform. Segmentation into meaningful units was performed using SegmentAnt, followed by semi-automatic annotation of discourse markers with AntConc and subsequent manual verification. The main research methods employed in this study are corpus analysis and discourse analysis, which made it possible to identify and interpret the features of the use of discourse markers in Chinese consumer goods advertising on the Internet platform Pinduoduo. title: Cognitive and discursive models of the ambivalent representation of artificial intelligence in American media discourse
text_snippet: Cognitive and discursive models of the ambivalent representation of artificial intelligence in American media discourse This article examines the ambivalent representation of the concept ‘artificial intelligence” in American media discourse. The relevance of this study stems from the need to identify the mechanisms underlying the formation of an ambiguous axiological and ambivalently interpreted image of artificial intelligence amid rapid technological development and its active mediatization. The aim of this study is to identify and describe the main cognitive and discursive models of the ambivalent representation of artificial intelligence, as well as to determine the linguistic means through which the positive and negative components of its media-discursive image are conveyed. The research material consisted of authentic texts from contemporary American media discourse devoted to artificial intelligence, its technologies, capabilities, limitations, and the social consequences of its application. The study employed a set of methods, including descriptive, contextual, discursive, cognitive, semantic, component, axiological, and interpretative analysis, as well as elements of quantitative analysis. title: The lexeme “security” in news discourse: from frequency to semantics (a corpus-driven study)
text_snippet: The lexeme “security” in news discourse: from frequency to semantics (a corpus-driven study) The article deals with a corpus-driven study of the lexeme security and its relevant word forms in English-language news texts aimed at developing analytical criteria that based on frequency characteristics reveal its semantic and pragmatic functions in the media discourse. The relevance of this research stems from the need for a comprehensive analysis of the concept security, identification of its functioning in contemporary media texts, and assessment of the pragmatic potential of the lexeme security in the dynamically changing information environment. The corpus approach is of particular importance as it enables the study of lexical items on the basis of a representative text collection, frequency patterns and collocations detection and specifics of contextual realization. The empirical material comprises an original balanced synchronic linguistic corpus of current CNN news texts for the period January 2025 – February 2026 of 120,942 sentences or over 3 million tokens totally. From this corpus 1,536 sentences containing 1,629 hits for the lexeme security were extracted. title: Cognitive resonance: dissonance as a pragmatic effect of polycode film text perception
text_snippet: Cognitive resonance: dissonance as a pragmatic effect of polycode film text perception This article explores the polycode nature of film texts, which underlies two types of pragmatic information perception: cognitive resonance as an enhancement of emotional impact resulting from the semantic correlation of the film’s verbal, visual, and auditory components, and cognitive dissonance as a weakening or problematization of the pragmatic effect caused by a conflict between semiotic codes. To verify qualitative observations, the study employs digital linguistics methods: automatic audio transcription (whisper model), audio parameter analysis (RMS loudness, spectral centroid) using the librosa library, and topic modeling of dialogues (LDA). These methods allow quantifying the effects of cognitive resonance and dissonance and presenting the results in a measurable, reproducible form. Using documentary films about the blind – the Russian “City of the Blind” (2009), the British “Notes on Blindness” (2016), and the feature film “Deadpool” (2018) – this article analyzes scenarios of resonant and dissonant interactions between semiotic codes. It demonstrates that the polycode nature is a key mechanism for conveying “foreign” experience in contemporary screen narratives.

title: Algorithmic Text Unification vs Egalitarian Digital Discourse
text_snippet: Algorithmic Text Unification vs Egalitarian Digital Discourse This study addresses the contradiction between the accessibility of online communication and the gradual simplification of national languages under the influence of digital mediatization processes. The relevance of the work stems from the need to overcome barriers to understanding meaning and protect the uniqueness of minority speech cultures from the algorithmic pressure of major network platforms. The empirical material includes the Russian-speaking communities of the Fediverse network, the decentralized blogging platform Bastyon, the secure Nostr protocol, as well as data from the Common Voice and Masakhane projects. Using texts in Russian, English, and African languages as examples, the paper thoroughly examines moderation rules, information distribution methods, and user speech behavior. The analysis confirms the negative impact of filter bubbles, which isolate audiences within homogeneous content and lead to the gradual disappearance of minority languages. It is established that the transition from centralized systems to decentralized environments eliminates algorithmic discourse distortion at the source code level. title: Antiphrasis as a Means of Indirect Speech Influence in Social Media Posts
text_snippet: Antiphrasis as a Means of Indirect Speech Influence in Social Media Posts This article examines the stylistic device of antiphrasis in modern online communication. Antiphrasis is a model of ambiguity in which a word, phrase, or sentence is used in a meaning opposite to its literal meaning, disguising a negative assessment with positive or neutral words. The paper emphasizes that antiphrasis is an effective tool for indirect speech influence, as it activates the addressee’s interpretive activity, forcing them to “complete” the hidden meaning. This study aims to identify and examine in detail the specifics of antiphrasis use in the social media. Particular attention is paid to analyzing its functional purpose and the variability of its implementation within the digital communication space. The relevance of this research stems from the extensive penetration of social platforms as a dominant channel of modern communication. This, in turn, stimulates the continuous evolution of language and generates innovative modes of linguistic expression, notably the intensified use of stylistic devices. title: Disability art in developing inclusive competence for intercultural communication specialists in the digitalization context
text_snippet: Disability art in developing inclusive competence for intercultural communication specialists in the digitalization context This study explores developing inclusion competence in future intercultural communication specialists by integrating work with works of art that present the theme of disability into the educational process. The relevance of this work stems from changes in contemporary Russian society, the digital transformation of education, and the search for one’s own identity, including the desire to understand certain key concepts within Russian tradition and culture. One concept requiring such understanding is disability. An analysis of the foreign language syllabi at Moscow State Linguistic University revealed that the topic of disability is not represented in educational materials. The authors propose integrating this topic into existing sections of the “Art” and “Culture” curricula. Using a comparative analysis of literary representations, the study describes the differences between Russian and Western models of understanding inclusion. title: Narrative Coherence in Native Advertising on the Dzen Platform (based on Travel Blogs)
text_snippet: Narrative Coherence in Native Advertising on the Dzen Platform (based on Travel Blogs) This paper examines the phenomenon of native advertising in travel blogs on the Dzen platform through the lens of narrative coherence – the ability of an advertising message to maintain internal consistency, logical flow, and naturalness within the author’s narrative. The methodological framework includes the descriptive and analytical method (to identify recurring integration patterns), integrated into algorithmic procedures for identifying advertising content based on semantic and syntactic analysis in the GATE environment using ANNIE Gazetteer, JAPE Transducer, and Java Regexp Annotator technologies, the typologization method (to develop a typology of native integration tools), content analysis of user comments, narrative analysis (to assess story coherence and consistency), as well as the comparative method. Based on an analysis of 114 partner publications from two popular blogs (“TrueStory Travel” and “Travels with a Camera”), three levels of advertising integration are identified: narrative strategies (personal experience, problem solving, testing, myth debunking), discursive formats (review, recommendation, roundup, repost), and commercial markers (links, promo codes, disclo

title: German ethnic adjectives deutsch and russisch as conceptual blends (based on the DWDS electronic corpus)
text_snippet: German ethnic adjectives deutsch and russisch as conceptual blends (based on the DWDS electronic corpus) The aim of this study is to describe the mechanisms of conceptual blending involving the German ethnic adjectives deutsch and russisch. Based on over 140 contexts extracted from the DWDS electronic text corpus of the German language, and employing the methodology of mental space theory and the blending concept by G. Fauconnier and M. Turner, combined with J. Pustejovsky’s qualia structure model, the mechanisms of integration of multiple mental spaces of ethnic words are analyzed. The synthesis of these approaches allows for the explication of deep semantic features actualized in discourse. It is revealed that ethnic adjectives, possessing a weak semantic structure and an extensive network of associative connections, actualize the agentive, constitutive, formal, and telic attributes of the qualia structure. It is established that the blends resulting from conceptual integration integrate different slots of the original mental spaces with specific associates, generating emergent meanings that are irreducible to the sum of the components’ meanings. title: Contextual usage of monetary unit names in modern German-language media corpus
text_snippet: Contextual usage of monetary unit names in modern German-language media corpus This study examines the use of currency denominations in a balanced linguistic corpus of news texts from “Focus”, Germany’s largest magazine. The relevance of the work is supported by the high interest in news discourse analysis within the linguistic community, as well as the objective need to develop mechanisms for identifying hidden manipulative influence on mass audiences through the media. The study textual material was transformed into an SQL database with a volume of over 1.7 million tokens using the Russian original software package “Balanced Linguistic Corpus Generator and Corpus Manager” (Rospatent Certificate No. 2023683209). The research utilized methods of automatic data collection, analysis of global currency data, corpus queries, quantitative analysis, and elements of discourse analysis (interpretation of contexts based on data from a broad discursive field). As a result, we obtained a subcorpus of 2,735 contexts containing the usage of currency names, compiled a frequency ranking, and conducted an in-depth qualitative analysis of the most common topics. title: Linguastatistical analysis of dominant meanings in the inaugural speeches of 21st-century leaders of the USA, the UK, and Russia
text_snippet: Linguastatistical analysis of dominant meanings in the inaugural speeches of 21st-century leaders of the USA, the UK, and Russia The paper presents a diachronic analysis of inaugural speeches delivered by the leaders of the United States, the United Kingdom, and Russia over the period 2000–2025, aiming to identify the evolution of lexical dominants in political discourse under the influence of global socio-political transformations. The relevance of the study is determined by the need to understand changes in the verbalization of state identity and speech strategies in the context of 21st-century global crises, including economic instability, the COVID-19 pandemic, and increasing international tensions. Political discourse is considered as a tool for constructing social reality and shaping collective values in conditions of global turbulence. The research material comprises a corpus of 20 inaugural speeches by leading political figures of the three countries, selected according to genre specificity, temporal framework, and political-discursive significance. title: Corpus approach to the interpretation of constitutive locative objects in the novella “The Hobbit, Or There and Back Again” by J. R. R. Tolkien
text_snippet: Corpus approach to the interpretation of constitutive locative objects in the novella “The Hobbit, Or There and Back Again” by J. R. R. Tolkien This study is devoted to a corpus-based analysis of the literary space representation in J. R. R. Tolkien’s novella “The Hobbit, or There and Back Again”. The relevance of the research is due to the need to refine the theoretical foundations for describing locative categories in literary texts and to further develop corpus linguistic methods for the analysis of literary works. The material of the study is the original text of the novella organized into a balanced linguistic corpus comprising 5,648 contexts (sentences) or 113,650 tokens. The lexical units “mountain”, “river”, and “lake” were selected as the objects of analysis, representing the basic types of locative organization in the fictional world. The study employs methods of corpus analysis, contextual and semantic analysis, as well as descriptive analysis. title: Corpus-based modelling of the cognitive-discursive matrix of teacher professional identity
text_snippet: Corpus-based modelling of the cognitive-discursive matrix of teacher professional identity The aim of the study is to develop and test a corpus-based model for reconstructing the cognitive-discursive matrix of teacher professional identity. Professional identity is interpreted as a discursively represented configuration of linguistic, conceptual, terminological, pragma-axiological and metaphorical parameters. The empirical basis of the study is a specialised corpus of English-language professional pedagogical discourse comprising more than 2,700 pages and over 2 million word tokens. The corpus includes written and oral materials: monographs, textbooks, research and popular-science articles, lectures, and professional educational texts. The research methodology combines digital text preprocessing, frequency analysis, reconstruction of dominant concepts, analysis of terminological density, pragma-axiological modelling, and identification of conceptual metaphors. The study established that the core of the teacher’s cognitive-discursive matrix is formed by six dominant concepts: “education”, “language”, “culture”, “identity”, “research”, and “method”. title: Digital strategies for museum content adaptation and the phenomenon of plain language
text_snippet: Digital strategies for museum content adaptation and the phenomenon of plain language This study explores contemporary digital strategies for adapting museum content and analyzes the phenomenon of plain language as a primary tool for enhancing information accessibility. Amidst the growing societal demand for inclusivity and clarity, museums are compelled to rethink traditional approaches to textual communication. The relevance of this research is underscored by the 21st-century imperative for museums to align with the principles of inclusion and universal design, ensuring that cultural heritage is accessible to the widest possible audience. The research methodology encompasses a theoretical analysis of relevant scientific literature on plain language linguistics and museum communication, alongside an empirical review and testing of digital tools. The article examines the fundamentals of the plain language approach and its application in real-world museum practices. Particular attention is given to digital instruments that measure text complexity and offer suggestions for improvement. title: Quantitative and statistical correlation of Cyrillo-Methodian, Preslav, and east Slavic lexis in Slavic miscellanies of the 11th–13th centuries
text_snippet: Quantitative and statistical correlation of Cyrillo-Methodian, Preslav, and east Slavic lexis in Slavic miscellanies of the 11th–13th centuries In order to identify the reflection of book traditions in seven Slavic miscellanies of the 11th–13th centuries — the Codex Suprasliensis, the Miscellanies of 1073 and 1076, the Uspensky, Troitsky, and Tolstovsky miscellanies, and the Miscellanies of the 13th century — a statistical analysis was carried out on nineteen pairs of synonymous words serving as markers of the Cyrillo‑Methodian, Preslav, and East Slavic scribal schools. To compare the widely varying token frequencies of lexemes across the miscellanies, a normalized weighted frequency method was used. This method consists of computing the term frequency (TF) of a word in a document, applying inverse collection term frequency (ICTF) weighting, normalizing the resulting TF×ICTF product by the maximum value of that word across all miscellanies, and then summing and averaging the normalized indices for words belonging to each tradition. The resulting value was interpreted as the tradition index for the given miscellany. title: Comparative analysis of audio descriptions and art‑historical descriptions: a corpus‑based study
text_snippet: Comparative analysis of audio descriptions and art‑historical descriptions: a corpus‑based study The study is devoted to a comparative analysis of the linguistic features of audio descriptions and art‑historical descriptions of art works. The analysis results revealed significant differences in the morphosyntactic characteristics of the texts. title: Assessing text complexity in Russian as a foreign language: an LLM-based approach and algorithmic toolkit
text_snippet: Assessing text complexity in Russian as a foreign language: an LLM-based approach and algorithmic toolkit The paper presents a toolkit and an algorithm for assessing the lexical complexity of educational texts used in teaching Russian as a Foreign Language (RFL). In the context of educational digitalization, the relevance of this issue is driven by the need for objective, scalable tools to calibrate the complexity of learning materials. The study employs computational linguistics methods, including a custom Python script (process_word_lists) and large language models such as GLM 4.6, Grok 4 fast, Claude Sonnet, GPT-5, and Gemini 2.5 Pro. The research material comprises two text datasets: (1) a training set, which includes standardized RFL lexical minimums and 268 educational texts spanning levels A1–C1 (according to the CEFR), and (2) a test set consisting of 26 reading texts at levels A2–B1. Expert evaluation and statistical metrics—specifically Cohen’s kappa, Mean Absolute Error (MAE), ordinal accuracy, and nominal accuracy—were used to evaluate classification quality.
